RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday, the December 16, 2002/Agrahayana 25, 1924 (Saka)

(Ministries:  Commerce and Industry; Development of North Eastern Region;

Total number of questions—20
109
Ban on animal testing
*361. SHRI MUNAVVAR HASAN:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that production of
anti-snake venom has been stopped;
(b) whether ban on animal testing is
creating hurdles in research and
development efforts Pharmaceutical
companies  in the country;
(c) if so, the manner in which the
companies are now supposed to test the new
medicines; and
(d) the action proposed to help  the
Indian companies which are compelled to
plan animal testing abroad?
Production of  commercial vehicles
*362. SHRI S. AGNIRAJ: Will the
Minister of HEAVY INDUSTRIES AND
PUBLIC ENTERPRISES be pleased to
state:
(a) the total production of commercial
vehicles in this financial year, model-wise;
(b) the total turnover of these units;
(c) whether there is any growth in the
production;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) the total value of export earnings
through export of such vehicles?
Expansion of SCTMI
*363.  SHRI V.V. RAGHAVAN:
SHRI J. CHITHARANJAN:
 Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the steps taken to expand and
improve the Sree Chithira Thirunal Medical
Institute and Research Centre (SCTMI) at
Thiruvananthapuram during the years from
1999 to April 2001; and
(b) whether Government propose to
provide enough money to equip SCTMI
with all the latest instruments required for
diagnosis and treatment in the Cardiology
and Neurology Departments?
Funds for various schemes to
Karnataka
*364. DR. VIJAY MALLYA: Will the
Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND
EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have received

any request from State Government of
Karnataka  for release of funds for
(i) Scheduled Caste children whose parents
are engaged in unclean occupations like
tanning, scavenging of dry latrines etc.,
(ii) Schedule Caste students for acquisition
of books under the Book Bank Scheme,
(iii) incentives for inter-caste marriages
(iv) to provide compensation to Scheduled
Caste victims of atrocities; and
(b) the present stage of consideration of
the request and by when funds are likely to
be released?
Government offices outside Delhi
*365. SHRI RAMACHANDRA
KHUNTIA: Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether  Government had decided
long back to shift several Government
offices outside Delhi to various cities of
National Capital Region in order to reduce
congestion in the Capital;
(b) if so, the number of such offices and
organisations identified for shifting out of
Delhi and how many  of them have been
shifted, so far;
(c) whether some of these identified
offices like, Coast Guard HQ are yet to be
shifted completely;
(d) if so,  the reasons therefor; and
(e) the steps taken by Government to
ensure full compliance of their orders in the
matter?
Telengiri Irrigation Project
resettlement plan
*366. SHRIMATI SUSHREE DEVI:
SHRI B.J. P ANDA:
 Will the Minister of TRIBAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the Telengiri Irrigation Project located in the
Koraput district of Orissa is awaiting
clearance from Government for
rehabilitation and resettlement plan;
(b) whether Government are also aware
that on completion, this will irrigate a vast
tribal area and drought-prone blocks of the
region; and
(c) if so, the present status of the case?
Drug licensing powers
*367. SHRIMATI AMBIKA SONI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
 Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government  approached
the States with a proposal that it would take
away the drug licensing powers currently
vested with them;
(b) if so, whether this proposal for
centralized licensing system for both drug
manufacturing and trade alongwith a Central
vigilance system would help to solve many
of the vexing regulatory issues;
(c) whether this proposal was placed at the
meeting of Health Ministers and Secretaries
of certain major States held in New Delhi in
the first week of November, 2002;
(d) if so, the decisions arrived at; and
(e) the steps being taken to implement them?
Assistance to NGOs operating in
Chhattisgarh and M.P.

BHENDIA: Will the Minister of TRIBAL
AFFAIRS be pleased  to state:
(a) the amount provided to voluntary
organisations for implementing the schemes
relating to Adivasis through TRIFED in
Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh; and

List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Monday, the December 16, 2002/Agrahayana 25, 1924 (Saka)
————
(Ministries:  Commerce and Industry; Development of North Eastern Region;
Disinvestment; Health and Family Welfare; Heavy Industries and Public
Enterprises; Information and Broadcasting; Law and Justice; Shipping;
Social Justice and Empowerment; Tribal Affairs; Urban Development and
Poverty Alleviation)
Total number of questions—155
551
Establishment of industries for
agricultural labourers
2514. SHRI R. KAMARAJ: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
a sizeable population of many districts of
our country are entirely dependent upon
agriculture and their sufferings increase
during monsoon failures;
(b) if so, whether Government will come
forward to start industries to provide
employment opportunities to those
unemployed agricultural labourers at the
time of monsoon failure; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Establishment of Rice Port
2515. SHRI S. M. LAL JAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have received representations for the
establishment of a Rice Port to facilitate rice
export;
(b) the details of the representations;
(c) whether  it is a fact that there is a
great potential for exporting rice to other
countries; and
(d) the measures Government propose
to exploit this potential?
Contract farming
2516. DR. ALLADI P. RAJKUMAR:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Tobacco
farmers are opposing the move to introduce
contract farming and are in favour of
retaining the present production and auction
system;
(b) if so, whether Government have any
proposal in this regard; and
(c) if so, the details in this regard?
Revival of cement factories
†2517. SHRI BASHISTHA NARAIN
SINGH: Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to sell
all cement factories which are running in
loss;

(b) if so, the norms prescribed for this
purpose; and
(c) if not, whether Government have
considered the measures to revive and
provide more funds to them, if so, the details
thereof?
Implementation of Labour in EPZs
and SEZs
2518. SHRIMATI CHANDRA KALA
PANDEY: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) the units in the Export Processing
Zones and Special Economic Zones
exempted from implementation of Labour
Laws;
(b) the details of the laws which are not
applicable in the EPZs and SEZs in the
country; and
(c) the measures taken by Government
to ensure implementation of Labour Laws
and protect the workers?
Import of edible oil
†2519. SHRI JANESHWAR
MISHRA: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
propose to import edible oil on a large scale;
(b) whether it is also a fact that both
traders and farmers are opposing this move
since this would ruin their market; and
(c) if so, the decision taken in this
regard?
News-item "India loses WTO cases
against European Union"
2520. PROF. M. SANKARA-
LINGAM:
SHRI PARMESHWAR
KUMAR AGAR WALLA:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the news-item captioned "India
loses WTO case against European Union",
which appeared in the Indian Express,  dated
the 6th November, 2002;
(b) if so, the details thereof and how
would Government defend WTO cases in
future;
(c) if so, the detailed study undertaken
in this regard; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Decrease in FDI
2521. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTA-
CHARJEE:
SHRI MANOJ BHATTA-
CHARYA:
SHRI P. PRABHAKAR
REDDY:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the total amount of Foreign Direct
Investment  (FDI) in the country during the
last three years, year-wise and sector-wise;
(b) whether there is perceptible decrease
in FDI;
(c) whether Government have instituted
any inquiry with regard to this matter;
(d) if so, the results thereof; and
(e) the steps being contemplated to attract
FDI in different sectors?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

RAO:

curbs on FDI from certain countries on
security grounds;
(b) if so, the details in this regard along
with names of the countries, the regions
and sectors identified for the purpose;
(c) the total FDI during the last five years
from the identified countries, year-wise,
